portraits.name: James Joyce
portraits.quote: He wanted to cry quietly but not for himself: for the words, so beautiful and sad, like music.
facts: Ulysses (1922) unfolds over a single day — 16 June 1904, now celebrated as Bloomsday.
The physicist Murray Gell-Mann named the quark after a line in Finnegans Wake.
Spent most of his adult life abroad, writing about Dublin.

portraits.name: Miriam Toews
portraits.quote: There must be satisfaction gained in accurately naming the thing that torments you.
facts: Grew up in the Mennonite town of Steinbach, Manitoba.
Women Talking became a 2022 film that won the Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay.
A Complicated Kindness won the Governor General's Award for Fiction (2004).

portraits.name: Toni Morrison
portraits.quote: We die. That may be the meaning of life. But we do language. That may be the measure of our lives.
facts: The first Black woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1993) — this quote is from her Nobel lecture.
Worked as an editor at Random House before her own novels took over.
Beloved won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1988.
Co-founded the Hogarth Press with her husband, Leonard, first printing books by hand at home.
The line on this bookmark comes from “Craftsmanship,” a 1937 BBC radio talk — the only known recording of her voice.
Mrs Dalloway (1925) follows a single day in London.
portraits.name: Virginia Woolf
portraits.quote: Words do not live in dictionaries; they live in the mind.

facts: Created Bertie Wooster and his unflappable valet, Jeeves.
Wrote more than 90 books over a career of more than 70 years.
The line on this bookmark, from The Code of the Woosters (1938), gave new life to the word “gruntled.”
portraits.name: P.G. Wodehouse
portraits.quote: I could see that, if not actually disgruntled, he was far from being gruntled.

portraits.name: Tom Stoppard
portraits.quote: Words are sacred. They deserve respect. If you get the right ones, in the right order, you can nudge the world a little.
facts: Born Tomáš Sträussler in Czechoslovakia.
Co-wrote the Oscar-winning screenplay for Shakespeare in Love (1998).
The Real Thing (1982) is a play about a playwright — and about getting words exactly right.

portraits.name: Brian Friel
portraits.quote: We name a thing and — bang! — it leaps into existence!
facts: Translations (1980) is set in 1833 Donegal, as British soldiers rename Irish places for a map — the line on this bookmark is spoken there.
Co-founded the Field Day Theatre Company with the actor Stephen Rea.
Dancing at Lughnasa (1990) won the Tony Award for Best Play.

portraits.name: Oscar Wilde
portraits.quote: Mere words! Was there anything so real as words?
facts: Won Oxford's Newdigate Prize for poetry as a student.
Wrote one novel: The Picture of Dorian Gray (1890).
Wrote more than 120 plays, of which only seven survive complete.
Aristotle held up his Oedipus the King as a model tragedy.
Also served Athens as a general, alongside Pericles.
portraits.name: Sophocles
portraits.quote: A little word hath often marred, or made, men's fortunes.

facts: Is credited with the earliest recorded uses of hundreds of English words, among them “lonely” and “bedroom.”
The line on this bookmark is said of a pair of show-off scholars in Love's Labour's Lost.
The same play contains “honorificabilitudinitatibus,” the longest word in his works.
portraits.name: William Shakespeare
portraits.quote: They have been at a great feast of languages and stolen the scraps.

portraits.name: T.S. Eliot
portraits.quote: For last year's words belong to last year's language / And next year's words await another voice.
facts: Worked at Lloyds Bank in London while writing The Waste Land.
His Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats became the musical Cats.
Won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1948.

portraits.name: Tom Waits
portraits.quote: I like to think that my main instrument is vocabulary.
facts: Earned an Oscar nomination for his score to One from the Heart (1982).
Was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2011.
Writes many of his songs with his wife, Kathleen Brennan.

portraits.name: Emily Dickinson
portraits.quote: I know nothing in the world that has as much power as a word.
facts: Fewer than a dozen of her nearly 1,800 poems were published in her lifetime.
Her family's 1844 Webster's dictionary was such a constant companion that scholars call it her lexicon.
The quote on this bookmark comes from one of her letters.

portraits.name: Vladimir Nabokov
portraits.quote: Form a habit of searching with unflinching patience for the right word.
facts: Wrote his novels first in Russian, then in English, and translated his own work.
A serious butterfly expert, he worked at Harvard's Museum of Comparative Zoology.
Saw letters in colours — a form of synaesthesia he described in his memoir, Speak, Memory.
Born Ricardo Eliécer Neftalí Reyes Basoalto; he took his pen name as a teenager.
Won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971.
Wrote odes to everyday things, from tomatoes to his socks.
portraits.name: Pablo Neruda
portraits.quote: Everything exists in the word.

portraits.name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
portraits.quote: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
facts: Published just one book of philosophy in his lifetime, the Tractatus (1921).
Gave away the fortune he inherited.
Spent several years teaching at village schools in rural Austria.

portraits.name: Gloria Anzaldúa
portraits.quote: Wild tongues can't be tamed, they can only be cut out.
facts: Borderlands/La Frontera (1987) moves between English, Spanish and Nahuatl, sometimes within a sentence.
Co-edited This Bridge Called My Back (1981) with Cherríe Moraga.
Grew up in the Rio Grande Valley of South Texas.

portraits.name: Confucius
portraits.quote: If names be not correct, language is not in accordance with the truth of things.
facts: His followers gathered his teachings into the Analects.
“Confucius” is a Latinised form of Kong Fuzi, “Master Kong.”
Taught philosophy at Oxford before and alongside writing 26 novels.
The Sea, the Sea won the Booker Prize in 1978.
Her life with the critic John Bayley was told in his memoir Elegy for Iris and the 2001 film Iris.
portraits.name: Iris Murdoch
portraits.quote: The fundamental distinctions can only be made in words. Words are spirit.

facts: Lived for two years and two months in a cabin he built by Walden Pond.
His essay “Civil Disobedience” influenced Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr.
Worked in his family's pencil business and improved the pencils it made.
portraits.name: Henry David Thoreau
portraits.quote: A written word is the choicest of relics.

portraits.name: Henry Hazlitt
portraits.quote: If you do not know the words, you can hardly know the thing.
facts: Wrote Thinking as a Science, where this quote comes from, at just 21.
Best known for Economics in One Lesson (1946).
Was a journalist for The New York Times and Newsweek.
Has written more than 20 books, on walking, hope, disasters and more.
Her essay “Men Explain Things to Me” (2008) helped inspire the word “mansplaining.”
Lives in San Francisco, the subject of her atlas Infinite City (2010).
portraits.name: Rebecca Solnit
portraits.quote: You can use the power of words to bury meaning or to excavate it.

facts: Published her first novel, White Teeth (2000), at 24.
Has taught creative writing at New York University.
The line on this bookmark comes from “That Crafty Feeling,” a talk about how she writes.
portraits.name: Zadie Smith
portraits.quote: I can change the whole nature of the thing by changing a few words.

facts: Won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1957.
Born in French Algeria, the setting of The Stranger (1942) and The Plague (1947).
Edited the Resistance newspaper Combat during the Second World War.
portraits.name: Albert Camus
portraits.quote: To misname an object is to add to the misery of this world.

portraits.name: Joan Didion
portraits.quote: The ability to think for one's self depends upon one's mastery of the language.
facts: Kept notebooks all her life, and wrote an essay, “On Keeping a Notebook,” about why.
Borrowed the title of Slouching Towards Bethlehem (1968) from a line of Yeats.
Won the National Book Award for The Year of Magical Thinking (2005).
